CONTEXT. These are notes headed 'Abel'sche Functionen August und September 1855'. The previous page and this one work with Riemann's canonically dissected surface T. Each handle ι gives a 'rectangle' with corners (ι,1),(ι,2),(ι,3),(ι,4). There are p normalized everywhere-finite integrals u_1..u_p. The aim is to build second-order (iterated) integrals ∫2u_{ι'}du_{ι''}, find their behaviour on the cuts, and then derive period relations for them by integrating around the whole boundary of T. This is the next level up from the bilinear relations for the u themselves.

(1) NORMALIZATION (lines 1-2). Across one cut, u_{ι'}^{(ι,2)} - u_{ι'}^{(ι,1)} = b_{ι,ι'}, with b_{ι,ι'} = 0 for ι≠ι' and b_{ι,ι} = πi. Across the other cut, u_{ι'}^{(ι,3)} - u_{ι'}^{(ι,1)} = a_{ι,ι'}, with a_{ι,ι'} = a_{ι',ι}. So the period matrix is (πi·I | A) with A symmetric, exactly the normalization of Riemann's theta series Σ exp(Σ a m m + 2Σ m u).

(2) SIDE INTEGRALS OF 2u'du'' (lines 3-4). I abbreviate b' = b_{ι,ι'}, a'' = a_{ι,ι''}, u''_1 = u_{ι''} at corner (ι,1).
- Along the side (ι,1)→(ι,2): ∫2u'du'' = b'(2u''_1 + b'') + b'a'' − b''a' + b_{ι,ι',ι''}.
- Along the side (ι,1)→(ι,3): ∫2u'du'' = a'(2u''_1 + a'') + a'b'' − a''b' + c_{ι,ι',ι''}.
These lines define the constants b_{ι,ι',ι''} and c_{ι,ι',ι''}. Riemann writes the sign in front of the third term as ∓; it must be − for the stated antisymmetry. My check: integrating by parts, ∫2u'du'' + ∫2u''du' = [2u'u''] = 2a'u''_1 + 2a''u'_1 + 2a'a'' along (1→3), and similarly with b along (1→2). Hence b_{ι,ι',ι''} = −b_{ι,ι'',ι'} and c_{ι,ι',ι''} = −c_{ι,ι'',ι'}. These agree with the explicit definitions on the previous page.

(3) NORMALIZED SECOND-ORDER INTEGRAL. Riemann sets πi W_{ι',ι''} = πi∫2u_{ι'}du_{ι''} − Σ_ι u_ι b_{ι,ι',ι''}.
- The jump of ∫2u'du'' along a cut is not constant; it is affine in u'' (its differential is 2·(jump of u')·du''). Riemann therefore records the jumps at the corner (ι,1).
- Since u_κ jumps by πiδ_{ικ} across the (ι,2)-(ι,1) cut, the subtracted sum removes b_{ι,ι',ι''}: W^{ι,2} − W^{ι,1} = b'(2u''_1 + b'') + b'a'' − b''a'.
- Across the other cut the constant becomes a_{ι,ι',ι''}, defined by πi a_{ι,ι',ι''} = πi c_{ι,ι',ι''} − Σ_{ι'''} a_{ι,ι'''} b_{ι''',ι',ι''}. This gives W^{ι,3} − W^{ι,1} = a'(2u''_1 + a'') + a'b'' − a''b' + a_{ι,ι',ι''}.
- Asserted: a_{ι,ι',ι''} = −a_{ι,ι'',ι'}, which is immediate from the antisymmetry of b and c. Also asserted: a_{ι,ι',ι''} = a_{ι',ι'',ι}, which is proved at the bottom of the page.
- The marginal note 'T^{ι'} mit T^{ι''} zu verbinden, (ι',1) mit (ι'',1)' fixes the connecting cuts between the p rectangles, joining the corners (·,1).

(4) SECOND-KIND INTEGRAL v (middle block). v has periods (0,…,0 | b_1,…,b_p) and is infinite at one point, where u_ι = β_ι. Its local behaviour is lim (u_ι − β_ι)v = γ_ι, so v du_ι ≈ γ_ι d log(u_ι − β_ι).
- On the boundary of T, v jumps by 0 across one cut and by b_ι across the other.
- The boundary pairs give ∫_{1}^{3} + ∫_{4}^{2} = 0 and ∫_{3}^{4} + ∫_{2}^{1} = b_ι b_{ι,ι'}. Summed over ι this is b_{ι'}πi.
- Riemann writes ∫v du_ι = −γ_ι(2)πi + b_ι πi. This is the residue-versus-periods (Riemann bilinear) relation for a second-kind integral against a first-kind one. It gives b_ι proportional to γ_ι (b_ι = 2γ_ι if the factor is 2πi).
- He then defines ε_{ι,ι'} = ∫_{ι,1}^{ι,2} v du_{ι'} and πi W_{ι'} = πi∫v du_{ι'} − Σ ε_{ι,ι'}u_ι. W_{ι'} is a third-kind-type function with a logarithmic singularity γ log(u − β). Its cut is drawn from (ι,1) to the pole ('(ι,1) mit v=∞ verbinden').
- Jumps: W^{ι,2} − W^{ι,1} = 0 and W^{ι,4} − W^{ι,3} = 2γ_ι b_{ι,ι'}, i.e. 2πiγ from the logarithm. Also W^{ι,3} − W^{ι,1} = W^{ι,4} − W^{ι,2} = γ_ι(2u_{ι'}^{ι,1} + a_{ι,ι'}) + g_{ι,ι'}, with g expressed through β, γ, a, b and Σγ b_{··,·}/πi as on the previous page.
- He starts ∫W_{ι'}du_{ι''} around ∂T: the second side pair gives γ_ι∫_{1}^{2}2u'du'' + b''(γ_ι a' + g). This computation is continued on the previous folio.

(5) THIRD-ORDER RECIPROCITY (bottom half). W_{ι',ι''}du_{ι'''} is finite everywhere, so its integral around the whole boundary of T vanishes. For each ι Riemann computes the two side-pair contributions.
- On the pair (1→3, 4→2) the integrand difference is −∫_{ι,1}^{ι,3} J(P)du''', where J(P) = 2b'u''(P) + const is the jump of W. Inserting the line-4 formula for ∫_{1}^{3}2u''du''' gives −b'a''(2u'''_1 + a''') − b'(a''b''' − a'''b'') − b'c_{ι,ι'',ι'''} − a'''(…).
- Analogously for the pair (3→4, 2→1) using ∫_{1}^{2}, giving terms a'b''2u''' + a'b_{ι,ι'',ι'''} + b'''a_{ι,ι',ι''} + ….
- Summing over ι and using b_{ι,κ} = πiδ_{ικ} and a symmetric, all u-dependent and cubic period terms cancel. For example, Σ_ι(−b_{ι,ι'}a_{ι,ι''} + a_{ι,ι'}b_{ι,ι''})2u''' = πi(a_{ι'',ι'} − a_{ι',ι''})2u''' = 0 (my check).
- What remains is: 0 = −πi c_{ι',ι'',ι'''} + Σ_ι a_{ι,ι'} b_{ι,ι'',ι'''} + πi a_{ι''',ι',ι''}.
- Comparing with the definition of a_{ι',ι'',ι'''} (step 3, using a_{ι,ι'} = a_{ι',ι}) gives a_{ι''',ι',ι''} = a_{ι',ι'',ι'''}. This is the cyclic symmetry written at bottom right.
- With the antisymmetry in the last two indices, a_{ι,ι',ι''} is totally antisymmetric (my inference; Riemann states only the two generating relations). It therefore vanishes identically for p ≤ 2.

In modern terms: Riemann defines quadratic periods of iterated integrals of holomorphic differentials relative to a canonical dissection. He normalizes them by subtracting a linear combination of the u, and proves a reciprocity law for them by Stokes/boundary integration around T, in parallel with the bilinear relations.
errors: Lines 3-4: the sign written '∓' before b_{ι,ι''}a_{ι,ι'} (resp. a_{ι,ι''}b_{ι,ι'}) must be read as '−'; only then are b_{ι,ι',ι''} and c_{ι,ι',ι''} antisymmetric, and this matches the explicit definitions on the previous page.

Middle block: the boundary integral of v du_ι is written −γ_ι πi + b_ι πi in the transcription. By the residue theorem the residue term should be 2πiγ_ι up to orientation; the image may contain the factor 2. In either case the coefficient/sign relating b_ι and γ_ι is not unambiguously fixed on the page.

The jumps of W_{ι'} across the (ι,2)-(ι,1) and (ι,4)-(ι,3) pairs are given as 0 and 2γ_ι b_{ι,ι'} here, but as −γ_ι b and +γ_ι b on the previous page. This is not a contradiction: it reflects a different placement of the cut to the logarithmic point. Readers should not mix the two sets of formulas.

In the first evaluation of ∫W_{ι',ι''}du_{ι'''} the parenthesised constant appears as (b'b'' − b'a'' + b''a'). The corner jump formula gives (b'b'' + b'a'' − b''a') if the side difference is taken as W(shifted) − W. The sign depends on orientation and Riemann's leading minus. Several partial lines are struck through, so the intermediate bookkeeping is unreliable, though the final relation is consistent.
Total antisymmetry of a_{ι,ι',ι''} is not stated explicitly; only cyclic symmetry and antisymmetry in the last two indices are written (these imply it).

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann systematically defines iterated integrals ∫(∫ω_i)ω_j of holomorphic differentials and normalizes them. He then derives a boundary-integration reciprocity law at second order, yielding totally antisymmetric triple constants a_{ι,ι',ι''}. Quadratic periods and harmonic volume are usually associated with Chen, Gunning, Harris and Pulte in the 1970s-80s. The method is a natural extension of his own bilinear-relation technique and the page is unfinished, exploratory scratch work with no stated application. I am unsure whether historians have already noted these computations in the 1855 notes. So this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a major new attribution.
